Unstable ranking (tau=0.158) + high correlation (0.845) + diagnosis says robust; DBA is a different robust mechanism than trimmed_mean (iterative drop vs rank-trim)
Test whether error-proportional weighting beats robust averaging when ranking is unstable (tau=0.158). Strong trend (0.96) should reward trend-tracking models via lower error weights.

Per-horizon top-k (k=5) on smape-ranked pool of 7; tests whether adapting weights across the 12-step horizon helps given unstable cross-window rankings (tau=0.158) and different window champions (ARIMA vs ONLY_CWT_catboost).

Caruana forward-selected complementary pool (THETA, catboost, ONLY_CWT_catboost, NaiveSeasonal) with inverse-error weighting; tests whether a smaller diverse pool with NaiveSeasonal for seasonality beats the top-7 per-horizon leader
Robust central tendency across all 19 models; tests whether equal-weight median beats error-weighted approaches given unstable ranking (tau=0.158) and correlated error groups

Per-horizon top-3 on full pool: unstable ranking suggests different models dominate at different horizons; wider pool lets each horizon pick its best from all 19 models including cross-cluster diversity
Smooth softmax weighting on the successful pool4; tests whether gradual per-model emphasis (vs hard topk) better handles unstable ranking and seasonal structure

Isolate pool-restriction effect: median is robust to unstable ranking (tau=0.158) and avoids weight-estimation variance on only 3 windows; compares against weighted-pool4 leaders to see if the gain is from the subset or the weights.
Unstable ranking (tau=0.158) and robust hint suggest equal-weight mean on the 7-model pool4 avoids overfitting weights to 3 windows; tests if weighting adds value over simple averaging
Robust combination on the winning 7-model pool: trims extreme forecasts to mitigate unstable ranking and correlated-error risk, distinct from plain mean and median already tested on this pool.

DBA optimizes per-horizon linear weights; with unstable ranking (tau=0.158) and different models winning at different windows, this could capture horizon-specific strengths better than a static mean. Strong seasonality (0.667) means different models may be best at different seasonal phases.

decision.justification: Selected 'mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9312. Series context: trend strength 0.9648 and seasonal strength 0.6668; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.158); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.713.
